title: Autotune circuit breaker and safety runbook for Optimize autoscaler
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: After the Feb autotune rollout for Optimize's batching/cache recommendations, we observed a spike in tail latency for a subset of low-concurrency customers when aggressive prefix caching and larger batch sizes were applied. This ticket captures a recommended circuit-breaker based runbook, mitigations already implemented, and follow-up engineering tasks to make safe applies and automatic rollback robust for future autotune runs.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-05: Autotune job (optimize/autotune/v2) recommended new batching/caching profile to ~150 customers; canary fraction roll started (5%).
- 2025-02-07: Canary telemetry showed increased p99 latency for the low-concurrency segment; autotune continued due to lack of strict safety gating in apply pipeline.
- 2025-02-08 03:40 UTC: Rollout reached 30% and multiple customer alerts fired. Ops paused rollout and applied emergency rollback to previous profile.
- 2025-02-08 05:20 UTC: Rollback completed; most signals back to baseline within 45 minutes.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- The autotune recommendation engine did not sufficiently model low-concurrency latency regimes: its cost-optimization objective prioritized batching gains without penalizing scenarios where queueing increases tail latency.
- The apply pipeline lacked a conservative circuit-breaker: rollout progressed based on host-level health checks and overall request success rate rather than segmented p99 latency for impacted cohorts.
- No preflight simulator executed against a synthetic low-concurrency workload to validate tail latency under new config.

Mitigations performed during incident:
- Immediate rollback to last-known-good batching/caching profile for affected customers. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/4321)
- Temp enforcement of an upper bound on batch_size for low-concurrency tiers via feature-flag to reduce queueing.
- Added a short-term alert that fires on cohort p99 latency degradation >30% over 15m. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/optimize/autotune-incidents

Runbook / Circuit-breaker design (proposal):
- Canary stage must include segmented SLO checks: compare p50/p95/p99 for 3 predefined cohorts (low-concurrency, bursty, high-throughput).
- Automatic rollback triggers: any cohort p99 increase > 20% vs baseline for 10m OR error rate increase > 1% sustained for 5m.
- Progressive apply policy: 0% -> 2% -> 5% -> 15% -> 40% -> 100% with a mandatory observation window (10–30m) between steps. Failing a step triggers immediate rollback to previous profile and pauses autotune for 24h for that model/workload combination.
- Safe-apply preflight: run a synthetic traffic simulation (local perf harness) that mimics cohort traffic for 20m sandboxed against a staging cluster configured with the candidate profile. The simulation must include KV cache hit/miss patterns and KV warmup behavior.
- Checkpointing: on apply, snapshot the runtime config + model variant mapping into the autotune history store with a human-readable ticket reference and automated diff. This enables deterministic rollback and audit.
- Operator overrides: expose a one-click abort/rollback in Console targeting a rollout id with automated dependency graph visibility (which customers affected, which regions).

Automated safety validators (to implement):
- Latency estimator: a lightweight estimator that predicts p99 change given candidate batch_size, cache_policy, and observed concurrency distribution. If estimated p99 delta > 10%, mark candidate as high-risk.
- Regression tests: add 3 targeted e2e tests in CI that run a 5-minute synthetic low-concurrency scenario against the autotune candidate profile. These tests must gate promotion to canary.
- Canary scoring: compute a multi-metric risk score (latency delta, token-cost reduction, error-rate delta, KV hit ratio change). Only candidates with score >= threshold progress. Thresholds tuned from historical incident corpus.

Action items (owners and tickets):
- Implement circuit-breaker logic in rollout engine (owner: Liam) -> sub-issue ENG-15892.
- Add synthetic preflight harness and CI gating (owner: Priya Singh) -> sub-issue ENG-15894.
- Build latency estimator and risk-scoring service (owner: Marco Diaz) -> sub-issue ENG-15896.
- Console: one-click rollback UI + rollout visibility (owner: Dana Park) -> sub-issue PM-401 (frontend + product).
- Retro: run post-incident blameless review with stakeholders and update autotune SLO definitions (owner: Aisha) -> meeting scheduled 2025-03-03.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
1) Rollout engine rejects or halts candidate profiles that fail segmented p99 checks or risk threshold.
2) Preflight simulator runs are required and green for all candidates promoted beyond canary.
3) Rollback action is executable from Console and completes in under 10 minutes for affected cohorts.
4) Documentation: runbook published in Confluence with step-by-step incident playbook and run commands. (Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Autotune+Safety+Runbook)

Longer-term considerations:
- Extend autotune model to include latency-penalized reward functions (explicitly encode p99 and tail-sensitive terms).
- Explore adaptive canary sizes: for smaller customers maintain very conservative batch targets automatically.
- Integrate model fingerprinting: certain model architectures historically sensitive to batch increases should be flagged and handled differently.

- Canary telemetry dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/optimize/autotune-canary
